source_review.notes: Checked all eight structured references at the official PostgreSQL, Oracle/MySQL, Microsoft, MongoDB, and Oracle Data Pump documentation URLs; each returned HTTP 200. Claims about PostgreSQL snapshot synchronization/import and COPY, InnoDB statement/transaction read views and DDL limits, SQL Server statement- versus transaction-level versioning, MongoDB point-in-time snapshot/history behavior, Oracle SCN export, and PostgreSQL vacuum responsibilities match the cited primary sources and are explicitly scoped by engine/version.

evidence: Checked source cut c, visible scope R_c, partition predicates q_i, partition rows R_{c,i}, logical identity K(r), schema fingerprint sigma_c, files F_i, manifest M_c, pointer P, change position l_c, and duration variables for stable meanings.
Draft chapter validation accepted every required heading and all GitHub-compatible inline/display mathematics delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Database snapshot, schema contract, partition coverage, immutable output, publication pointer, and CDC position remain distinct throughout.

evidence: Executed the annotated Python fixture: four rows at cut 10 total 100, two partitions are disjoint/exhaustive, mixed lower@10 plus upper@11 totals 95 and matches no represented cut, two receipts publish, duplicate receipt is idempotent, and missing validation does not publish.
Recomputed Exercise 2: committed totals are 200 at cuts 20 and 21, while mixed cuts produce 210 and 190 around the cross-range transfer.
Recomputed Exercise 3 using decimal units: 12,000,000 MB / 250 MB/s = 48,000 s = 800 min; plus 30 min, times 1.5, equals 1,245 min = 20 h 45 min, exceeding 16 h by 4 h 45 min.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit row counts, sums, partition counts, duration conversions, and publication predicates reproduce.

evidence: Verified the indicator condition sum_i 1[q_i(r)]=1 for every r in R_c implies both exhaustive coverage and pairwise exclusion for all exported source rows.
Verified the two-inclusion argument: worker completeness adds every R_c member and source-cut/predicate admission prevents out-of-scope members, yielding the disjoint-union equality.
Verified independent cuts invalidate the theorem premise even with stable disjoint key predicates because a committed cross-range invariant can be partially observed.
Verified publication P:M_old->M_c is conditional on exact expected partitions, matching cut/schema, immutable file integrity, and snapshot-level controls.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The algebra models logical visibility and set coverage; it does not assume physical row order, universal isolation semantics, or transaction-free source cost.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The ten examples and five exercises span consistency, partitioning, topology, schema, source safety, serialization, publication, security, restore, and continuity boundaries.

evidence: Checked explicit object/row/security scope, one engine-proven source cut, synchronized workers, fixed schema/session settings, stable read-only deterministic queries, and honest fuzzy-scan labeling.

Checked disjoint/exhaustive planned predicates including empty outputs, same cut/schema per receipt, immutable attempts, one accepted receipt per partition, exact manifest membership, and validation-before-pointer publication.
Checked source connections/time/transaction age/I-O/version store/replica lag/retention thresholds, safe cancellation, prior-generation preservation, and same-cut-only retry.
Checked source-position pairing for CDC, compatible-cut reconciliation, least privilege, secret/PII retention controls, and no inference from exit code/counts alone.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants connect source visibility, logical coverage, serialized integrity, and dataset publication without collapsing them into one dump-tool outcome.

evidence: Reviewed the partition theorem and confirmed it requires one fixed R_c, exact-one predicate membership, complete worker reads, and no output outside source scope.
Reviewed cross-range transfer counterexamples in the compact example and Exercise 2; mixed cuts violate conservation while both individual committed cuts preserve it.
Reviewed the publication argument: missing/extra/wrong-cut/wrong-schema/corrupt partitions cannot enter the trusted pointer under the stated validator and conditional update premises.
Reviewed the duration calculation boundary so planning arithmetic is not presented as a throughput guarantee or permission to exceed source history limits.
proof_review.notes: Deductive results are conditional on source and worker premises; empirical controls cannot manufacture an engine guarantee that is absent.

evidence: The set-coverage result is labeled theorem with a two-inclusion proof and its premises stated adjacent.
The mixed-history construction is labeled counterexample, while schema, holder, immutable-attempt, publication, source-impact, and handoff statements are labeled conditions/invariants.
Engine behavior is attributed to specific primary documentation and explicitly prohibited from universal cross-engine inference.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter distinguishes mathematical set implications, database contract premises, operational policies, finite tests, and provider-specific facts.

evidence: The executable model is explicitly limited to four rows, two represented cuts, two range partitions, and in-memory receipts/publication.
Counts, keys, digests, source controls, restored samples, and performance observations are bounded to named fields/cuts and accompanied by blind spots.
Logical snapshot validation is separated from physical restore drills, external-source consistency, historical completeness, and future execution behavior.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production isolation, metadata visibility, version retention, durability, security, impact, and restore fitness require engine- and deployment-specific evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the distinctions among statement and transaction snapshots, snapshot identifier and durable position, synchronized and independent readers, logical and physical extraction, data and schema visibility, partition coverage and workload balance, per-file integrity and snapshot publication, and baseline consistency versus ongoing CDC continuity.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable source inventory, engine cut acquisition, PostgreSQL-style holder/import ordering as a scoped example, range/hash plans, worker receipts, type/session fidelity, source abort thresholds, same-cut retry, manifest/pointer publication, compatible-cut reconciliation, restore drills, credential/data controls, and CDC handoff.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review motivates mixed-history failure; exposition follows scope, cut, engine semantics, partitioning, serialization, impact, validation, publication, recovery, and continuity; notation supports the exact-cover proof; the runnable example reproduces an impossible mixed total; and ten examples plus five solved exercises cover distinct design decisions.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local execution were checked on 2026-09-02. The finite model and documented examples do not establish any deployed engine's isolation, metadata/DDL visibility, snapshot lifetime, cross-node consistency, version-store behavior, source impact, logical serialization fidelity, physical restorability, access policy, storage durability, privacy compliance, publication atomicity, or CDC continuity; those require engine-specific contracts and production evidence.
